title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are buzzing with activity, from launch contracts to new patents in space data management. Meanwhile, the regulatory landscape is shifting as commercial launch licensing faces potential environmental exemptions.

themes.title: Launch Contracts Galore
themes.body: Rocket Lab's recent contract win from Japan's iQPS and SpaceX's $1.6 billion in military satellite launch orders highlight a robust demand for launch services. This trend suggests that the appetite for satellite deployment continues to grow, particularly in defense applications.

themes.title: Patents and Data Centers
themes.body: Sophia Space and Caltech's patent for space data centers signals an emerging focus on data management in orbit. As the volume of space-based data increases, so too does the need for innovative solutions to handle it.

themes.title: Regulatory Shifts Ahead
themes.body: A proposed rule to exempt commercial launch licensing from environmental regulations could streamline operations for launch providers. However, this move may raise eyebrows among environmental advocates, setting the stage for a potential clash.

themes.title: IPO Delays and Defense Demand
themes.body: L3Harris's decision to postpone its missile business IPO to 2027 reflects the complexities of capitalizing on surging defense demand. This delay may indicate a cautious approach amid market volatility and evolving defense priorities.
